 Petrol, Diesel Prices Today, November 17, 2026: Check Latest Rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru 
 Authored By HDFC SKY | Published at: Nov 17, 2026 09:36 AM IST

 Mumbai, November 17: Petrol and diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities on Tuesday, November 17. Petrol retailed at Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi and Rs 111.21 in Mumbai, while diesel was priced at Rs 95.20 and Rs 97.83 per litre, respectively.    
 The Centre has increased the windfall gains tax on exports of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) for the fortnight beginning November 16, while retaining the levy on petrol exports at zero.   
 The special additional excise duty (SAED) on diesel exports, along with road and infrastructure cess, has been raised to Rs 14 per litre from Rs 11.50 per litre. Similarly, the levy on ATF exports has been increased to Rs 12.50 per litre from Rs 11 per litre. The duty on petrol exports remains unchanged at zero.   
 The Finance Ministry announced the revised rates through a late-night notification on November 16, with the changes taking immediate effect. The government has been revising these levies every fortnight since introducing export duties on diesel and ATF in March amid escalating tensions in West Asia and a surge in international crude oil prices.   
 The windfall tax regime is aimed at ensuring adequate domestic availability of petroleum products by discouraging excessive exports when international prices make overseas sales more lucrative. The latest revision, however, does not affect the existing duty structure on petrol and diesel sold in the domestic market.   
 Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday, November 17, as expectations of a global supply surplus and recovering Middle Eastern exports outweighed concerns over continued attacks on oil tankers and energy infrastructure in the Gulf region.   
 Brent crude futures fell 0.7% to $91.8 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) declined 0.6% to $85.2.   
 The decline follows a sharp fall in the previous session, when Brent settled 3.6% lower at $92.44 per barrel and WTI dropped 3.2% to $85.72. Investors have increasingly shifted their focus towards improving global supply prospects, even as geopolitical risks continue to threaten shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.   
 Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade, said the market was increasingly accepting that oil supply had caught up with demand and could potentially exceed it. The changing supply-demand balance has emerged as the primary factor weighing on crude prices, taking precedence over geopolitical concerns.   
 The International Energy Agency (IEA) said last Friday that the global oil market would return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026, as Middle Eastern exports recover faster than global demand despite continued attacks on shipping.   
 According to the agency, global oil supply is expected to average 105 million barrels per day (bpd) during the quarter, exceeding projected demand by 1.7 million bpd. The IEA had previously anticipated a supply deficit for the period.   
 However, the improving supply outlook remains vulnerable to disruptions. Attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz have continued, keeping uncertainty elevated around one of the world’s most important oil-export routes.   
 Waterer said the geopolitical risk premium associated with the US-Iran conflict had not disappeared but was currently taking a back seat to expectations of higher supply.   
 Meanwhile, the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) held an online meeting on Monday to review members’ maximum sustainable production capacities. The exercise will help determine production quotas for OPEC+ members in 2027 and beyond.   
 The wider OPEC+ group, which includes allies led by Russia, is scheduled to meet on November 29 to decide its oil production policy for 2027.   
 In the US, crude inventories held in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell to 276.4 million barrels last week, their lowest level since August 1982, according to the Department of Energy. The recent drawdowns are part of an agreement to release 172 million barrels from the reserve.   
 For India, lower international crude prices offer some relief on the import bill and inflation front, given the country’s heavy dependence on imported energy. However, continued instability in the Gulf and any disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remain key risks to the outlook.   
 Check the latest petrol and diesel rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and other cities.   
 Petrol Prices   
 Petrol prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Tuesday, November 17, with no revision in retail fuel rates. In New Delhi, petrol was priced at Rs 102.12 per litre, while consumers in Mumbai paid Rs 111.21 per litre and those in Kolkata paid Rs 113.51 per litre.   
 Among other metropolitan cities, petrol retailed at Rs 107.76 per litre in Chennai and Rs 111.68 per litre in Bengaluru. Hyderabad continued to have one of the highest petrol prices at Rs 116.15 per litre, while Thiruvananthapuram recorded a rate of Rs 115.49 per litre.   
 In northern India, petrol was priced at Rs 102.97 per litre in Gurugram, Rs 101.96 in Noida and Rs 101.89 in Lucknow. Jaipur and Patna recorded higher rates of Rs 113.19 and Rs 113.37 per litre, respectively, while Chandigarh had one of the lowest prices at Rs 101.54 per litre.   
 Among other state capitals, petrol was retailing at Rs 108.97 per litre in Bhubaneswar. Oil marketing companies revise petrol and diesel prices based on international crude oil prices, currency movements and other market factors. However, retail rates remained steady across all the cities listed on Tuesday.   
 Diesel Prices   
 Diesel prices remained unchanged across major Indian cities and state capitals on Tuesday, November 17, with no revision in retail rates. In New Delhi, diesel was priced at Rs 95.20 per litre, while consumers in Mumbai paid Rs 97.83 per litre and those in Kolkata paid Rs 99.82 per litre.   
 Among other metropolitan cities, diesel retailed at Rs 99.55 per litre in Chennai and Rs 99.56 per litre in Bengaluru. Hyderabad recorded a price of Rs 104.23 per litre, while Thiruvananthapuram had the highest rate among the listed cities at Rs 104.40 per litre.   
 In northern India, diesel was priced at Rs 95.64 per litre in Gurugram, Rs 95.44 in Noida and Rs 95.36 in Lucknow. Jaipur and Patna recorded rates of Rs 98.25 and Rs 99.36 per litre, respectively, while Chandigarh had the lowest price among the listed cities at Rs 89.47 per litre.   
 Among other state capitals, diesel was retailing at Rs 100.68 per litre in Bhubaneswar. Oil marketing companies determine retail diesel prices based on international crude oil prices, currency movements and other market factors. However, rates remained unchanged across all the cities listed on Tuesday.
